body: ### Fixes from Opus review #### **Blockers** * **`get a sanitizer config from options` step reordering**: Restructured the algorithm so `sanitizerSpec` is initialized upfront and correctly handled across all branches (`TrustedParserOptions` $\rightarrow$ `options["sanitizer"]` $\rightarrow$ unsafe check $\rightarrow$ built-in safe default fallback). * **`createContextualFragment()` owner document**: Added a step to adopt `fragment` into `contextDocument` before returning from the fragment parsing algorithm, preserving the expected node document. * **Adoption Agency Algorithm parentless `lastNode`**: Added a check that `lastNode`'s parent is non-null before removing, and reset `lastNode` to null. * **"in head" script insertion location**: Added an optional `overrideLocation` parameter to *insert an element at the adjusted insertion location* and passed `adjustedInsertionLocation` at the call site. * **`NotSupportedError` & context assert**: Removed the unreachable `NotSupportedError` throw; moved the assert that `context` is non-null before returning `null` when sanitizing a `

From https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/62492#issuecomment-5572776961 > `sanitizer-in-adoption-agency.sub.dat:125-134` — `
TextMore
` with `div` replaced is a three-way disagreement. The expectation is `TextMore`, Chrome gives `TextMore`, and I read the spec as giving `TextMore`, since `map[div]` is set to `(b, null)` when the `
` is replaced and both the AAA "Keep" insertion and the later `` resolve through it. The relevant test was: ``` #data
TextMore
#config { "replaceWithChildrenElements": ["div"] } #document | | "Text" | | | "More" ``` Any thoughts on what should happen here?

The above comment was from an older revision of this PR, and the current revision should produce `TextMore` which matches Chromium. However, I asked Claude to compare Chromium's implementation with this PR for this case, and it found there's still a difference if you insert another formatting element to the test: For the exact wpt case they agree, but only by coincidence, and the two use different mechanisms that diverge as soon as the inner loop does any work. `html_tree_builder.cc:1984-2000` (Chrome 155.0.8052.0 canary): ```cpp case Sanitizer::Action::kReplaceWithChildren: // Skip DOM operations. Children safely remain in furthest_block. continue; case Sanitizer::Action::kDrop: tree_.TakeAllChildren(new_item, furthest_block); break; case Sanitizer::Action::kKeep: case Sanitizer::Action::kKeepElement: tree_.TakeAllChildren(new_item, furthest_block); tree_.Reparent(furthest_block, new_item); break; ``` So `kDrop` is exactly keithamus's suggestion. But `kReplaceWithChildren` records nothing: Blink has no redirection map. `HTMLConstructionSite::Reparent` and `TakeAllChildren` both route through `AdjustInsertionLocation` (`html_construction_site.cc:1246-1285`, `:878-918`), which walks up the stack of open elements from the target, skipping items whose action is `kReplaceWithChildren`, and resolves the root through `root_insertion_point_`. That is a dynamic re-resolution at each insertion, where the spec stores a resolved pair in the map. In `
TextMore
` the inner loop breaks on its first iteration, so the nearest kept stack ancestor of `div` just is `commonAncestor` (`b` having been removed from the stack), and `source:148169` lands in the same place. Add a kept formatting element in between and they part ways: `
Textafter` with `{ replaceWithChildrenElements: ["div"] }` Canary: ``` | | | "Text" | | | "after" ``` Spec at `4edf8660`: `map[div]` exists, so `:148169` sets it to the adjusted insertion location given (`commonAncestor`, null), and `commonAncestor` is the root, so it resolves to the container. Both `newElement` and `"after"` then go to the container rather than into the cloned ``: ``` | | | "Text" | | | "after" ``` With `
Textafter` Canary puts them inside the cloned ``, so it really is the nearest kept ancestor, not `commonAncestor`. Canary looks right to me: the plain parse of that input puts the `div` inside the cloned ``, so `div`'s children should go there too. The redirect at `:148169` is standing in for the "append lastNode to node" that `:148089` suppressed by forcing `lastNode` to null when `furthestBlock` isn't "Keep", so it should point at the first "Keep" `node` the inner loop reaches (falling back to `commonAncestor` when the loop breaks immediately), not at `commonAncestor` unconditionally. Edit: fixed in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12756/commits/5452f09dcf06bdad93704b3098f5e06a838bded5

One more divergence from Chromium: `
Textafter` with `{ replaceWithChildrenElements: ["section"] }` After 8 iterations `section` is still the current node, and its redirection map entry is still `(div8, null)` from when it was inserted. Chromium's stack walk from `section` now finds `b^8` (inserted immediately below `div8`), so Canary gives: ``` |
(div8) | | "Textafter" ``` The spec as written gives: ``` |
(div8) | | "Text" | "after" ``` (In a normal parse, ["Textafter" is one text node in `section` in `b`](https://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/?%3Cb%3E%3Cdiv%3E%3Cdiv%3E%3Cdiv%3E%3Cdiv%3E%3Cdiv%3E%3Cdiv%3E%3Cdiv%3E%3Cdiv%3E%3Csection%3EText%3C/b%3Eafter).) More generally, the map entry of any replaced-with-children element directly below `furthestBlock` in the stack goes stale once `newElement` is inserted between them, but in every other case those elements get popped by the final outer iteration before they can be an insertion target again. I think the fix is to update the entries for the run of replaced elements immediately below `furthestBlock` after inserting `newElement` into the stack, pointing them at the adjusted insertion location given (`newElement`, null). Edit: fixed in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12756/commits/16e9bb577243335797ab1af26d66de8064651fbf

AI review Here's the consolidated picture, with Canary 155.0.8059.0 as the reference and each item verified by trace against the spec at 16e9bb57. **Spec problems** - **Foster parenting regression in the AAA, also without a sanitizer.** Main's "adjusted insertion location" re-ran "appropriate place for inserting a node" with the passed target, so `lastNode` at a table-ish `commonAncestor` was foster-parented. The PR's version at `source:145518-145524` uses the passed location verbatim, so `
xy` now moves the div into the table (Canary and main put it before). With `removeElements: ["table"]` the div, "x" and "y" vanish. Fix: at `source:148195` compute the appropriate place for inserting a node given `commonAncestor` and pass that in. The `newElement` step is fine, since main appended to `furthestBlock` directly. - **Custom element lookup isn't gated on the sanitizer.** "Create an element for the token" at `source:145410-145428` looks up the definition (and `is`) before sanitizing, and the fragment root carries the target's registry, so a dropped `` still gets an upgrade reaction and its constructor runs at the end of `setHTML`. Chromium skips the lookup for disallowed elements, and `sanitizer-custom-elements-constructor.html` already asserts that. Same for `is` removed by config: the spec builds the customized built-in, Canary makes a plain element. This is the existing XXX at `source:145419`. - **Noah's Ark wording.** `source:142357-142362` compares attributes "as they were when created by the parser". With attribute sanitization at insertion that reads as token attributes, which is what Chromium compares. Behavior matches; a note would settle it. **Chromium bugs, spec looks right** - Foster-parented replaced-with-children content goes into the table: `
x
y` replacing div gives `tr > ("x", td)` in Canary. Same with `ayc...` and the AAA variant `
xy` replacing div. Chromium walks the stack from the element rather than using its foster location. Non-streaming Chromium matches the spec. - Document-level comments and processing instructions survive `comments: false` in `parseHTML`/`parseHTMLUnsafe`, because `ShouldInsertChild` skips sanitization when the parent is a Document. - `parseHTMLUnsafe` with no sanitizer option drops in-tree comments, unlike `setHTMLUnsafe` and `DOMParser`. - `template` in `replaceWithChildrenElements` hoists template contents as light DOM (`ab` gives `"axb"`), including declarative shadow roots. The spec drops the contents. - Passing any options object to `setHTML`/`setHTMLUnsafe` flips Chromium to scripting-enabled parsing, so `

AI review Reviewed at `72ba4a98`, together with wpt#62492 at `1db3e5d`. I mostly looked at what changed since `906ddc15`: attributes are now sanitized when the element is created, there's a null registry for non-Keep elements, the inert document gets a registry, and the AAA has `bookmarkMoved`. **Blockers** - `source:145930-145934`: children of a replaced-with-children element look up their registry from the replaced element, because "appropriate place for inserting a node" doesn't redirect, so `intendedParent` is the replaced element. That registry is now null. So `div.setHTML('', {sanitizer: {replaceWithChildrenElements: ["span"]}})` on a disconnected `div` never constructs `x-foo`. Under a shadow root with a scoped registry, `x-foo` also gets the global registry when the fragment is adopted. Chromium resolves through to the real parent (`html_construction_site.cc:1269-1278`). Consider keeping the looked-up registry for "Replace with children" and only skipping the definition lookup, so a null registry is used only for "Remove". - `source:147129-147132` together with `source:151644`: a declarative shadow root on a *removed* host now gets the inert document's registry, which is the target's. So `setHTMLUnsafe('', {sanitizer: {removeElements: ["span"]}})` runs `x-foo`'s constructor on discarded content. That contradicts the note at 145937. Before this revision, the inert document's registry was null here. Consider using a null registry when the host's registry is null. **Suggestions** - `source:151644-151652`: the note's rationale doesn't seem to hold. `root` already gets the target's registry (151716), and top-level elements look up their registry from `root`. As far as I can tell, this step only changes the DSR registry above. That includes plain `setHTMLUnsafe()`, where a scoped target's registry is used instead of the document's global registry after adoption. It also adds the inert document to a scoped registry's scoped document set. Could it be dropped? If it's intentional, the commit message should say so. Also, "now" in the note reads like a changelog. - `source:151729`, `151776`: with the fragment created in the inert document, *all* parsed elements are now created in the inert document, not just top-level ones. This applies to plain `innerHTML` too. Steps that resolve a URL once against the node document now see `about:blank`, e.g. `div.innerHTML = '

'` ends up with no poster frame. Before, only top-level elements had this problem. Could the inert fragment be limited to sanitizing parses, or is this intended? - `source:146152-146158`: "Replace with children" with a `Document` target parent can't be reached: only the root `html` is inserted into a `Document`, and `html` is on the built-in non-replaceable list. Consider replacing it with an `Assert`. - *HTML fragment parsing algorithm* / in head `template` step (`hostIsRoot`, `source:147037`): `div.setHTMLUnsafe('

> AI review

Good catch — switched to using `declarativeShadowHostElement`'s own custom element registry, matching what `attachShadow()` does when no `customElementRegistry` is passed. This also handles the sanitizer case without a special check: a host that will be removed was created with a null registry, so its shadow contents get no registry and no constructors run. Added a note to that effect.


> **Setting the inert document's registry**

Agreed, and dropped.

Reviewed at `7dec21df`, covering `5bdc4612`, `ae18e134` and `7dec21df` since `d5dcf0ca`, together with wpt#62492 at `ddc809a9`. The spec changes look right:
- The DSR registry is back to the host's node document's registry, and the note's claim holds: the inert document and the `parseHTML*()` `Document` both have a null registry.
- The safe default now goes through configure, `remove unsafe` and the validity assert.
- The wording nit is fixed.
- The wpt bugs are fixed, the `.tentative` names are dropped, and most of the coverage gaps now have tests.

**Suggestions**
- `source:147041`: using the current node as the declarative shadow host is normative for every fragment parse, not just sanitizing ones. It matches Chrome Canary 157, Fx Nightly 160 and Safari TP (`div.setHTMLUnsafe('<template shadowrootmode=open>x</template>y')` gives no shadow root and 2 children). Consider mentioning it in the commit message.

The observable difference is coalescing of text nodes" and "MDN … N/A, no behavior change". AI feedback Reviewed at 25ae90c, together with web-platform-tests/wpt#62492. Lint passes and the build succeeds. The issues raised in earlier rounds look fixed at this head: the processing-instruction allow-list, the `html`/`body` attribute merges, replaced `template`, the AAA `lastNode` and foster-parenting cases, the `script`/`template` insertion overrides, and the declarative shadow root registry. **Blockers** - [*sanitizer config allows an attribute*](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/25ae90c515e167d0f2d1216112e7221a2aa82ba3/source#L129434) uses *elementName* in its navigating-URL and animating-URL steps ([L129434](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/25ae90c515e167d0f2d1216112e7221a2aa82ba3/source#L129434), [L129444](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/25ae90c515e167d0f2d1216112e7221a2aa82ba3/source#L129444)), but never defines it. The algorithm only gets *elementLocalName* and *elementNamespace*. As written, the `javascript:` URL checks can't be evaluated. Adding "Let *elementName* be «[ "name" → *elementLocalName*, "namespace" → *elementNamespace* ]»." after *attrName* fixes it. - [*insert a foreign element*](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/25ae90c515e167d0f2d1216112e7221a2aa82ba3/source#L146209) now computes the insertion location before *create an element for the token*, and inserts at that same location afterwards. In document parsing, creating the element can run script: a microtask checkpoint, a synchronous custom element constructor, or `attributeChangedCallback`. Main recomputed the location after creation. For example: ```html ``` `x-foo` is foster-parented with location (`body`, `table`). The constructor removes the table, so the insertion is before a node that is no longer a child of `body`, which violates the *ensure pre-insert validity* assertion. Main appended `x-foo` to `body`. Using *insertionLocation* only for the intended parent, and calling *insert an element at the adjusted insertion location* with just *element* as main did, would fix this. The [`script`](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/25ae90c515e167d0f2d1216112e7221a2aa82ba3/source#L146939) and [`template`](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/25ae90c515e167d0f2d1216112e7221a2aa82ba3/source#L147037) start tag steps follow the same pattern, though there only customized built-ins can run script. - The [*HTML fragment parsing algorithm*](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/25ae90c515e167d0f2d1216112e7221a2aa82ba3/source#L151743) now creates every parsed element in the inert document, not only top-level ones. This includes `innerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML()`, `createContextualFragment()`, and `setHTMLUnsafe()` without a sanitizer. Some steps resolve a URL against the node document when an attribute is set and don't re-run on adoption: media `src` ([L38973](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/25ae90c515e167d0f2d1216112e7221a2aa82ba3/source#L38973), "when the src attribute was last changed") and `poster` ([L37251](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/25ae90c515e167d0f2d1216112e7221a2aa82ba3/source#L37251)). The inert document's base URL is `about:blank`. So per spec, `div.innerHTML = '

'` no longer loads the video or gets a poster frame. Top-level elements already had this problem on main. - The PR description lists the inert creation as intended, but not this fallout. - #11669 is still open on whether legacy methods should parse into an inert document. - Consider limiting the inert fragment document to the parses that need it (non-Legacy mode, or a non-null configuration). Alternatively, first make media `src` and `poster` re-run on adoption, which `setHTML()` and `setHTMLUnsafe()` need anyway. **Suggestions** - Consider updating the PR description: - The MDN checklist item still says "N/A, no behavior change", which contradicts the "Web-observable changes" list. - The list doesn't mention these changes: - A declarative shadow root is only attached if the configuration keeps `template` and its `shadowrootmode` attribute. `template` is Uncategorized, so `setHTML()` with the default configuration no longer creates them; main attached them from the token and sanitized inside. `shadowroot*` attributes the configuration removes no longer apply either. - `

AI feedback Reviewed at 53c8837, covering 6624235 and 53c8837 since 25ae90c. Lint passes and the build succeeds. The earlier blockers are addressed. Only sanitizing parses use the inert fragment document now, so `innerHTML` and other parses without a sanitizer are back to main's behavior. Sanitizing parses still have the regression below. **Blockers** - Sanitizing parses still break media elements that the configuration keeps. - On main, `setHTML()` and `setHTMLUnsafe()` parsed into a fragment in the target's document, so nested elements were created there. Now every element of a sanitizing parse is created in the inert document, whose base URL is `about:blank`. - Media `src` ([L38973](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/53c8837cb2f6713314e401a01537bcfef205a5b7/source#L38973), "when the src attribute was last changed") and `poster` ([L37251](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/53c8837cb2f6713314e401a01537bcfef205a5b7/source#L37251)) resolve against the node document when the attribute is set, and don't re-run on adoption. - So per spec, `div.setHTMLUnsafe('

', {sanitizer: {}})` no longer loads the video, while the same call without a sanitizer does. This also affects every `innerHTML` on pages whose Trusted Types default policy returns a sanitizer from `createParserOptions`. - Making media `src` and `poster` re-run on adoption, here or in a prerequisite PR, would fix this, as well as the existing top-level case on main.

> **Blockers** > > * Sanitizing parses still break media elements that the configuration keeps. > > * On main, `setHTML()` and `setHTMLUnsafe()` parsed into a fragment in the target's document, so nested elements were created there. Now every element of a sanitizing parse is created in the inert document, whose base URL is `about:blank`. > * Media `src` ([L38973](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/53c8837cb2f6713314e401a01537bcfef205a5b7/source#L38973), "when the src attribute was last changed") and `poster` ([L37251](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/53c8837cb2f6713314e401a01537bcfef205a5b7/source#L37251)) resolve against the node document when the attribute is set, and don't re-run on adoption. > * So per spec, `div.setHTMLUnsafe('

', {sanitizer: {}})` no longer loads the video, while the same call without a sanitizer does. This also affects every `innerHTML` on pages whose Trusted Types default policy returns a sanitizer from `createParserOptions`. > * Making media `src` and `poster` re-run on adoption, here or in a prerequisite PR, would fix this, as well as the existing top-level case on main. This is an existing issue, I opened #13068, and it's actually something we should fix as part of #798. The streaming sanitizer reveals it in a new way but the issue exists for e.g. regular fragment parsing already.
